races.name: Community Engagement Programme Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hope Rising
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (411) with two wins over 16f and 12f on Good ground makes trip and surface ideal; Jamie Snowden's yard is in red-hot form at 2/2 over 14 days, Rob Hornby rides, and 7 days since last run suggests a fit, fresh horse — her natural prominence here is unchallenged and she races genuinely on-pace rather than out of role.
runners_data.comment: Hope Rising brings a sharp double to this contest, winning two of her last five starts with consecutive victories arriving just seven days ago, and she has experience of both today's trip and conditions — our rating of 69 marks her out as the one to beat, though the 135 lb burden is the one query.

runners_data.name: Sneaky Blinder
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane picks up the ride on a horse returning from 50 days off (headgear: p) for Robert Stephens whose yard has produced 0/3 in the past 14 days; only 1 from 15 runs on similar going is a significant concern, and the hold-up style leaves her entirely dependent on Hope Rising tying up in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Sneaky Blinder arrives here with distance and going experience to call on, and a win in his last six starts keeps him honest at 130 lb; the 50-day absence is the one factor to weigh up.

races.paceDynamic: Hope Rising is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this two-runner contest at Chepstow over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival capable of pressuring her early, she will dictate every fraction from the front on her own terms. Sneaky Blinder, a hold-up operator by style, will track at a respectful distance and rely entirely on a strong late run to reel in whatever lead Hope Rising constructs. With just two runners, this is functionally a match race — Hope Rising controls the tempo, the fractions, and the tactical shape throughout. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the prominent/front-running profile: a single uncontested leader setting a comfortable, metronomic gallop over 1m4f on fast ground can simply conserve energy and kick clear, leaving the hold-up horse with too much to do from off the pace if the leader has anything left in the tank.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hope Rising bowls along at a controlled, sustainable gallop and Sneaky Blinder cannot close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Hope Rising, never headed and never pressured, simply picks up the pace entering the straight and runs out the winner on her own terms; Good to Firm ground suits her profile (12/15 on similar going) and the unchallenged lead removes any energy cost from scrapping for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hope Rising sets a pace fractionally too hot in isolation and ties up in the final furlong, handing Sneaky Blinder a winning run.
scenarios.body: Sneaky Blinder, held up off a moderate lead by Loughnane, produces a sustained late run if Hope Rising has overcalculated her fractions and fades close home; one win from 15 on similar going makes this a low-probability but non-zero threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Match-Race Duel
scenarios.trigger: If Loughnane elects to challenge much earlier than expected and turns this into a genuine two-horse battle from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Forced out of her comfort zone earlier than ideal, Hope Rising could be vulnerable if Sneaky Blinder's trainer has freshened the horse (50 days off) into peak condition to make a forward move; Robert Stephens' recent trainer strike rate of 0/3 in 14 days mutes this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Void/Declared Over
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two runners is withdrawn at the start or fails to complete, reducing this to a walkover or no-contest.
scenarios.body: With only two declared runners any single withdrawal negates meaningful race shape; not a tactical scenario but a real field-size risk worth acknowledging at this small field size.

watchPoints.text: Hope Rising's unchallenged lead is the defining factor — watch whether Rob Hornby allows her to coast through early fractions or accidentally quickens them, which would determine whether Sneaky Blinder can close.

Sneaky Blinder has raced on Tapeta and Standard surfaces for her last three runs; the switch back to Good to Firm turf (only 1/15 on similar going) is a material concern for her ability to produce a meaningful late run.
Sneaky Blinder is returning from a 50-day absence for a yard that has hit 0/3 in the past 14 days — fitness and peak readiness must be questioned before siding with her in a two-runner match.
With only two runners declared, any veterinary withdrawal at the start would reduce this to a walkover — check the declaration board before race time for any late changes.
Hope Rising carries 135lbs against Sneaky Blinder's 130lbs; the 5lb weight concession is modest but worth factoring if this race becomes a close-run thing in the final furlong.

races.name: Trade Centre Group Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Bailey Family Investments / EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Trade Centre Wales Handicap Stakes (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Counting Cards
runners_data.note: Recent form is poor (7th-9th-9th over comparable trips and going) and the three-year absence from the winner's enclosure is a red flag; a natural hold-up horse displaced into the map's midfield, its chance depends on a strong late surge that the current form does not support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Counting Cards at least has experience of today's trip and conditions to call upon, and 35 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; the worry is that recent efforts have been consistently well beaten.

runners_data.name: Rating
runners_data.note: Promoted to the front by default as the sole confirmed pace-setter, which is actually its most dangerous role — five runs over this trip including a win on firm and three places on good suggest it handles the conditions well, though Rossa Ryan must judge the tempo astutely to avoid collapsing under late challengers.
runners_data.comment: Rattled off a win in her last six starts — a winner five starts back — and she arrives here fit on 25 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and ground and 132 lb from stall two; the worry is just one success in recent starts may leave her vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Risen Again
runners_data.note: John & Thys Flint's yard is 1/7 in the past 14 days, which is a mild positive angle; a genuine hold-up horse shown in midfield because the map is overloaded at the rear — its best recent effort was a 2nd over 10f on good ground, and stepping back to a flat mile on quicker ground looks a stretch.
runners_data.comment: Risen Again showed well when second last time out and returns here in good shape after just 16 days, with experience over today's trip and going a clear asset; the main concern is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Bobby Dassler
runners_data.note: Won over this exact course and distance on good ground (1/8f/GOO) and that form line stands out in a field of modest mile specialists; though naturally a hold-up operator whose position is shifted forward on the map, Mason Paetel (5lb claimer) must navigate the compression of hold-up types to find a clean run in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Bobby Dassler has finished seventh in each of his last two starts and ranks seventh of eight on our figures, making him hard to fancy despite a third and a win in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, and 21 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Ajrad
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's yard has been in solid form (2/23 over 14 days) and Ajrad has a consistent placed record over 7-8f on good ground (three of last five in the frame); races from hold-up territory but is nudged into midfield here — at OR 53 it is well enough weighted if the race develops into a staying finish.

runners_data.name: Scarfo
runners_data.note: Back-to-back placed efforts at 7-8f on good ground (2nd, 2nd, 3rd in recent starts) make this five-year-old one of the most consistent horses in the field; Bernard Llewellyn's yard is 1/7 in the past 14 days, Zoe Lewis claims 7lb, and the combination of recency, form, and weight allowance gives this horse a live each-way profile from wherever it ends up racing.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures in a field of eight, Scarfo is hard to fancy on a mark of 49, but he has run over today's trip and going before, and a return to form is not impossible given he showed a second two starts back and a second three starts back.

runners_data.name: Law Of Design
runners_data.note: Top weight at 135lbs alongside Look Back Smiling, but Ian Williams's yard is 3/38 over 14 days — an active and capable yard; Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking and Law Of Design's placed effort over this trip on good ground (5/8f/GOO) suggests it handles conditions, making it the most plausible horse to sit prominently and overhaul Rating late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Law Of Design has at least run over today's trip before and returns on a handy 24-day break, but a string of mid-pack finishes and 135 lb to carry make it hard to see him threatening from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Look Back Smiling
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand is an obvious class booking but the horse's form on good ground is thin (0 wins, 0 places from two runs on similar going) and it has been beaten out of the frame in its last two starts; its natural tendency to race from hold-up territory is a disadvantage in a race where the pace is unlikely to be fast enough to bring it into play in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Rating is the only confirmed front-runner in this field and, mapped to the lead by default, will set what figures to be a measured, uncontested pace over Chepstow's flat mile on Good to Firm ground — a surface that rewards horses who travel smoothly rather than those who need soft underfoot. With no genuine rival to press Rating into an injurious early gallop, the pace is likely to be honest but controlled, creating a falsely run or evenly-run contest that plays into the hands of horses who can sit close to the tempo and produce a sustained finish rather than a sharp late burst. This field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Counting Cards, Risen Again, Bobby Dassler, Ajrad, and Scarfo are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield on the map, meaning several will inevitably race closer to the pace than their handlers would ideally choose. The tactical verdict is clear: with a single, uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable tempo and the majority of the field bunched in midfield, horses who can race prominently just off Rating and produce a strong, staying finish through the final two furlongs hold the dominant positional advantage — prominent-to-midfield closers over a mile on this track are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rating Controls, Stays Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Rating dictates unchallenged from the front and the pace remains steady enough to sustain its effort to the line.
scenarios.body: Rating takes full advantage of the uncontested lead, settling into a rhythm and using the flat Chepstow mile to grind rivals into submission before they can close; on Good to Firm ground its five previous runs over this trip and course profile make it the most likely horse to see out the race from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Swamps Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Rating's pace proves just slow enough to allow a horse sitting second or third to overhaul it in the final furlong with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking Rating within a length or two enjoys the perfect racing position — sheltered from the wind, always travelling, and producing a finishing effort when the field stretches — while Rating, having led throughout, finds little extra under pressure; Law Of Design and Ajrad, both capable of racing closer than their natural style suggests, are the primary threats.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Rating fades sharply after halfway, creating a gap that a horse finding room off the turn can exploit.
scenarios.body: Scarfo has the form to finish powerfully (back-to-back placed efforts over this course and distance) and Risen Again has shown the ability to produce a late run on good ground; however, both are squeezed into midfield on the map rather than their natural rear position, meaning the ground they must make up is shorter than ideal for a true sprint-finish scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Rating sets an unusually slow early pace that bunches the entire field and produces a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: With eight horses effectively racing in a cluster, a genuine sprint finish over the final two furlongs becomes a lottery of positioning and luck in running; Look Back Smiling and Bobby Dassler, both capable on their best form, could benefit from a chaotic outcome — but neither has the course or going form to make this a reliable route to the frame.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rating's early fractions — if Rossa Ryan allows it to bowl along unchallenged, the race effectively becomes Rating's to lose and any horse not tracking it within two lengths faces a seriously compromised finish.

Scarfo with Zoe Lewis's 7lb claim is the stand-out each-way watch: four placed efforts from five recent starts over comparable trips, and the weight relief could bring it into genuine contention if it secures a clean passage from its compressed midfield position.

Law Of Design's booking of Billy Loughnane from the Ian Williams yard (3/38 in 14 days) signals stable confidence — watch for it to be ridden prominently from the outset rather than waiting, which would make it a dangerous rival to Rating.

Bobby Dassler's course-and-distance win on good ground is the single strongest form line in the race on paper — watch whether Mason Paetel attempts to use that track knowledge to slot into a closer position than the horse's natural style would suggest, which could be decisive.

The field is unusually loaded with hold-up types compressed into midfield; if the first two furlongs are slow, watch for a bunching effect turning for home that could result in interference, causing several fancied runners to lose their position at a critical moment.

races.name: Trade Centre Uk Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Espona Bay
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with a win over 7f on good ground 12 days ago and a strong recent form string including two wins; Kieran O'Neill takes the ride for Scott Dixon, and her similar-going record (5 runs, 1W2P) backs up her suitability, making her the most credible late challenger if pace develops sufficiently.
runners_data.comment: Espona Bay arrives on the back of a win last time out and has winning form in his last six starts, with experience over today's trip and going lending solid claims at 131 lb from stall 5; the fifth-place finish two starts back is the one blemish that gives rivals hope.

runners_data.name: Name The Day
runners_data.note: Oliver Carmichael claims 7lb for Eve Johnson Houghton, whose 14-day strike rate of 6/44 is modest; the 7f win on good ground is the key form pointer but the horse has only managed 4/5 in similar going overall and the erratic recent form (49104) raises questions about consistency — needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Name The Day showed smart form when winning three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her very much in the mix off a mark of 70; the fourth last time out is the obvious question to answer.

runners_data.name: Von Trotter
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this Michael & David Easterby-trained three-year-old who won over 7f on good ground 17 days ago and placed over 6f on the same surface; her 6/9 similar-going record includes 1W2P and prominent style suits tracking Evie Ross before challenging in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Von Trotter arrives in excellent nick, winning last time out and filling the runner-up spot two starts back, and his experience over today's trip and conditions bolsters his claims; the main concern is whether he can reproduce that sharp recent form from stall three carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Honky Tonk Girl
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane is a strong jockey booking for Oliver Cole, whose 14-day record is a lean 1/14; her only win came on firm going over 6f and her best form has come at that shorter trip — naturally a prominent racer, she is displaced into midfield by the field's composition and will need a messy race to get her preferred position and distance combination.
runners_data.comment: Ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Honky Tonk Girl faces a stiff task despite a win last time out, as her recent form is patchy — third and fourth in the two starts preceding that victory — though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a fresh enough 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Too Much Trevor
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by style who showed a 7f win on good ground in recent form, but Grace Harris has no wins from 14 runners in the last 14 days and Too Much Trevor's similar-going record over 15 runs reads just 1W5P — the pattern is of a horse who is placed rather than wins, and the apprentice allowance (Ashley Lewis, 3lb) is a minor compensation.
runners_data.comment: Hard to fancy ranked last of seven on our figures, Too Much Trevor has been out of the placings in one of his last three starts, and his speed rating of 55 gives little encouragement, though he does bring distance and going experience and returns fit on just nine days' rest.

runners_data.name: Evie Ross
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Clive Cox, who has a solid 14-day record of 6/20; the visor is noted, she ran well to win over 5f on good ground but her last five runs have all been over 6f and this step to 7f on faster ground is the central question — if she gets a soft lead Rossa Ryan will try to make it unassailable, but stamina over this trip is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Evie Ross shaped with promise when winning in her last five starts and has experience of today's trip and going, with her trainer firing at 30% over the past fortnight; drawn in stall one carrying 135 lb, she is the one to beat on an 85 rating.

runners_data.name: Rogue Exile
runners_data.note: Harry Davies partners this James Owen-trained three-year-old who has run only twice — a win over 7f on good ground and a close second at the same trip — giving an unbeaten/placed record on this exact trip and going combination (2/2, 1W2P); the lack of exposed form means connections will have confidence, and the prominent style suits racing just behind Evie Ross before delivering a challenge.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims, but our rating of 71 ranks him fifth of seven and he carries 134 lb from stall 2, which may temper expectations for this lightly tested colt.

races.paceDynamic: Evie Ross is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure likely from this seven-runner field, she should be able to dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the gates — a sustainable pace that keeps the tempo honest without burning herself out. Von Trotter and Rogue Exile are the main prominent challengers who will track close to the pace, creating a compact early order that denies room for late-charging hold-up horses to build a meaningful momentum swing. The field contains more pace-minded types than the map can accommodate cleanly — Honky Tonk Girl is a natural prominent racer forced into a midfield role, and while Too Much Trevor is a genuine hold-up type, the congestion in the early stages means neither is likely to settle into their ideal position. On a good-to-firm Chepstow seven furlongs where a controlled pace will reward those travelling smoothly in the first four, prominent to midfield runners who can quicken off a steady gallop — specifically Rogue Exile and Von Trotter — are best positioned to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Evie Ross Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Evie Ross sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and those travelling prominently track and quicken past her in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Evie Ross's unchallenged lead keeps fractions honest, meaning stamina is preserved and the race turns into a sprint from the two-furlong pole; Rogue Exile, with a perfect 1W2P record in similar going and only two career runs, and Von Trotter, fresh off a recent win over this trip on good ground, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally stronger than anticipated and the prominent horses tie up, creating a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Espona Bay has won over 7f on good ground and finished first in recent form, making her the most likely beneficiary if the race develops a strong enough gallop; Name The Day also has a 7f win on good ground but has been inconsistent, so depends on a genuine test to find form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Evie Ross Front-To-Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so controlled and fractions so slow that Evie Ross simply has too much gas left to be caught in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A field of seven over 7f on good-to-firm at Chepstow with no serious pace rival means Evie Ross could steal a lead that proves unassailable if the closers leave their runs too late; her one previous win came over 5f on good ground, so a 7f solo test on faster going is a genuine question mark, but Rossa Ryan's positive booking gives this shape a non-trivial chance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsiders Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate gallop concertinas the field and a horse racing outside its optimal position finds room to burst through at big odds.
scenarios.body: Honky Tonk Girl, though pushed out of her natural prominent position, has a win on firm ground and could benefit from a chaotic, bunched finish if gaps appear late; Too Much Trevor's hold-up style is also genuinely suited to a muddling race, but her trainer has 0 wins from 14 in the last 14 days and she has run nine times in similar going without a win in those conditions.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Exile has run only twice, both over 7f on good ground with a win and a place — if James Owen's 9/40 14-day strike rate reflects a stable in form, this lightly-raced horse's unexposed profile is the biggest danger to the forecast.

Honky Tonk Girl is a natural prominent racer who will be forced to settle in midfield — watch whether Billy Loughnane attempts to push forward early, which could increase the tempo and unsettle Evie Ross's rhythm.

Evie Ross is stepping up to 7f for the first time and wearing a visor — if the trip stretches her stamina in the final furlong, the horses immediately tracking her (Von Trotter, Rogue Exile) will be poised to sweep past without needing to make up extra ground.

Too Much Trevor ran just 9 days ago and has a high number of similar-going runs (15) without dominating — watch whether the short turnaround affects her finishing effort, as Ashley Lewis may be forced to switch ground late in a small, compactly-run field.

Name The Day has been dropped back from 8f to 7f and switches from a stamina test to a speed test — if Oliver Carmichael (7lb claim) settles her closer than usual given the steady pace, she may outrun her current inconsistent form.

races.name: Saxon Automobiles Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Savannah Smiles
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid course-and-distance form (won 6f on Good), handled by conditional Harry Vigors; needs a fast early pace to unleash her late run, which is not guaranteed with only Zoulu Warrior in front — the patiently ridden style is her strength but also her dependency here.
runners_data.comment: Savannah Smiles won three starts back and was second two starts back, but she was well held in sixth last time out, so there are questions about current form; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 135 lb from stall five are the key conditions she faces here.

runners_data.name: Le Beau Garcon
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up type who has been consistent at sprint trips on Good going but has not won recently; Joanna Mason takes over, and while the sim-going record is solid, he steps up from 5f to 6f and needs genuine pace to bring his finishing effort into play.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Le Beau Garcon nonetheless holds a rating of 69 against an official mark of 64, suggesting he retains untapped potential, and he arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call on; the risk is that his recent string of poor finishes makes an immediate turnaround hard to guarantee.

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent-racing mare in the Grace Harris yard who fits neatly into the pocket behind the leader; the tp headgear suggests she needs to be held together early, and four consecutive fourth-place finishes at 6f suggest she finds one or two ahead of her at the death.
runners_data.comment: Connie's Rose has been knocking on the door in recent starts, finishing second twice in her last six, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — her rating of 69 makes her a genuine second-string threat, though she remains winless and must convert consistency into something more.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Warrior
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and the pivotal horse in shaping this race; his last win came over 6f on Standard going and his form on Good turf has been modest — Lewis Edmunds must find a clean line at the start and manage fractions carefully to avoid being run down by the prominent pack.
runners_data.comment: Zoulu Warrior landed a win five starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid claims on conditions, while our rating of 66 edges his official mark; the worry is three consecutive disappointing efforts in his last three starts.

runners_data.name: Calafrio
runners_data.note: Dual-6f winner including on Good going, wearing tongue-tie and cheekpieces; Benoit de la Sayette is an upgrade in the saddle, and his natural prominent style means he is well positioned to be the primary beneficiary if Zoulu Warrior controls without extending himself.
runners_data.comment: Calafrio won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but she ranks eighth of ten on our figures and a speed rating of 61 does little to inspire confidence; the burden of 134 lb adds another reason to be cautious.

runners_data.name: Benavente
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old stepping sharply back in trip having run exclusively over 7f-12f on Tapeta recently; Nicola Currie takes the ride after a 144-day break, and while the OR of 59 gives a weight advantage, the trip and fitness question marks are significant concerns.
runners_data.comment: Benavente comes into this in fine fettle after winning last time out, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on; a 144-day absence is worth noting, but his rating of 77 marks him as the one to beat from stall one carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Vape
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent type with experience at 6f on Good, partnered by 7lb claimer Charlie Tucker; T14 form of 1/7 shows some recent activity, but at OR 57 and with modest recent form he is likely to fulfil a pacemaker-adjacent role rather than win.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Vape's best recent effort was a second five starts back, though a fourth two starts back hints at some ability; he has run over today's distance and going before, and returns after 33 days off carrying 128 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won over this exact C&D trip on Good going last time; Billy Loughnane (trainer's son) takes the ride and the horse is fit having run nine days ago — if the pace is strong enough to set up a late run, his course form makes him the most interesting of the closers.
runners_data.comment: Arnaz won last time out and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround, giving him fitness claims, and he has run over today's trip and going before; however, five modest efforts prior to that victory and a mark of 54 suggest he faces a stiff test off stall eight carrying 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Marisitta
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse by style and recent form (won 6f on Good, ran second at same trip) but mapped forward due to redistribution — her true race position will be further back than shown, and at OR 50 with a 3lb apprentice she needs everything to fall right; the style mismatch tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Marisitta faces a stiff task, though she does arrive on the back of a runner-up finish last time and has experience of today's trip and going; one win in her last six starts makes her hard to fancy at the weights with 121 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Some Nightmare
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer whose position in this field is crowded out by faster-breaking rivals; at OR 49 and nine years old, he has been placing consistently at 6f on Good but has not won this season, and the likelihood of being shuffled wider or further back than ideal dampens his prospects.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Some Nightmare sits near the foot of the ratings and faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround with some recent placed efforts to his name.

races.paceDynamic: Zoulu Warrior is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 10-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival willing to take them on from the gates — Calafrio, Benavente, and Vape all want to race prominently but none profiles as a gate-to-wire type that will seriously contest early supremacy. That creates a single-file, controlled gallop from the front with a four-runner cluster of prominent types — Connie's Rose, Calafrio, Benavente, and Vape — bunched behind, generating material traffic and positioning friction between the 2f and 3f poles on Chepstow's turning straight. The hold-up runners Savannah Smiles, Le Beau Garcon, and Arnaz will be last or near-last early, needing the pace to be genuinely honest for their late runs to land — and with one unchallenged leader that is not guaranteed on Good to Firm ground. This race shape most favours horses racing prominently in behind Zoulu Warrior, positioned to track a controlled pace and pounce from 2f out without needing a true sprint-collapse from the leader; the field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the map can accommodate cleanly, with Calafrio and Connie's Rose best placed to actually secure their natural prominent berths, while Some Nightmare and Marisitta — genuine prominent and hold-up types respectively — are likely to find themselves further back than they prefer.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zoulu Warrior Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Zoulu Warrior dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trio track efficiently without traffic trouble.
scenarios.body: Zoulu Warrior sets a sustainable fractions on Good to Firm ground, and the horses positioned just behind — Calafrio and Connie's Rose — have the shortest ground to cover turning in, allowing them to quicken past a tiring leader in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Opens Lane for Closer
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types collide for position early, causing interference and burning energy between 3f and 2f out.
scenarios.body: The positional scramble among Calafrio, Benavente, Vape, and Connie's Rose creates an uneven pace and leaves a gap in the final furlong that a well-timed hold-up horse can exploit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Stolen Clear, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Zoulu Warrior finds an even lower gear through the middle sections and the prominent pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Good to Firm ground suits a clean-jumping, front-running type, and if the chasing group is mired in traffic at the 2f pole, Zoulu Warrior's head start proves decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Sweep From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops from a prominent battle and conditions allow a sweeping late run to materialise.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the single confirmed front-runner setting a controlled gallop; only if the prominent scrimmage significantly elevates fractions would true hold-up horses arrive in time.

watchPoints.text: Prominent traffic between 3f and 2f out — with Calafrio, Connie's Rose, Benavente, and Vape all wanting the same ground, watch for checking, bumping, or a runner being forced wide on the turn into the straight.

Zoulu Warrior's early break — if he misses the kick or is headed immediately, the entire pace map collapses and a more chaotic, high-tempo race unfolds that would benefit the hold-up horses disproportionately.
Benavente's fitness after 144 days off and a trip contraction from 7f-12f to 6f; if she fades sharply inside the final furlong she could cause interference to horses challenging behind her.

Savannah Smiles and Arnaz — both hold-up types on the outer or rear — watch how quickly the pace develops in the first two furlongs, as that single factor determines whether either has a realistic chance of arriving in time on this flat but tight-finishing track.
